question: Can you figure out the average difference in pageviews between users who bought something and those who didn’t in December 2020? Just label anyone who was involved in purchase events as a purchaser.
sql:
WITH dec_events AS (
  SELECT 
    user_pseudo_id,
    event_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201201' AND '20201231'
),
purchasers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM dec_events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
),
user_pageviews AS (
  SELECT 
    user_pseudo_id,
    COUNT(*) as pageview_count
  FROM dec_events
  WHERE event_name = 'page_view'
  GROUP BY user_pseudo_id
),
all_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM dec_events
),
user_classified AS (
  SELECT 
    au.user_pseudo_id,
    CASE WHEN p.user_pseudo_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as is_purchaser,
    COALESCE(up.pageview_count, 0) as pageview_count
  FROM all_users au
  LEFT JOIN purchasers p ON au.user_pseudo_id = p.user_pseudo_id
  LEFT JOIN user_pageviews up ON au.user_pseudo_id = up.user_pseudo_id
)
SELECT 
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser = 1 THEN pageview_count END) as avg_purchasers,
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser = 0 THEN pageview_count END) as avg_non_purchasers,
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser = 1 THEN pageview_count END) - AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser = 0 THEN pageview_count END) as difference
FROM user_classified
